ARG.note: World's #1 soybean-meal exporter (USDA Oilseeds MY2024/25 ~27 Mt; 30-40% of global soymeal trade). ~345 crush plants, ~67 Mt crush capacity on the Rosario/Parana river complex. Crushes its own and Paraguayan/Bolivian beans into meal for the EU, Southeast Asia and the Gulf. Argentina exports far more meal than whole beans by policy design.

BRA.note: World's #1 soybean producer and #2 soybean-meal exporter (USDA: ~42.7 Mt meal production MY2024/25, ~21.6 Mt domestic use, ~21-23 Mt exports). The largest single supplier of soymeal to the EU (~7.9 Mt) and a major supplier to Southeast Asia. Domestic crush expanding with biodiesel mandates.

USA.note: World's #1 soybean-meal producer (~56 Mt) and #3 exporter at a record ~15.7 Mt (USDA MY2024/25), lifted by new crush capacity built for renewable-diesel oil demand which leaves surplus meal. Ships mostly to the Western Hemisphere (Philippines, Mexico, Colombia, Canada) and Southeast Asia.

IND.note: World's leading exporter of rapeseed (mustard) meal and a major groundnut/soybean-meal exporter. Solvent Extractors' Association: record ~4.9 Mt total oilmeal exports FY2023-24 (rapeseed meal ~2.2 Mt, soymeal ~2.1 Mt, plus castor/rice-bran). Main markets: South Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Bangladesh, the EU and Japan.

CHN.note: World's largest soybean crusher and soybean-meal consumer (~77 Mt domestic feed use), turning imported beans into meal for its vast hog and poultry sector. A small net exporter of finished meal to Japan and neighbours despite crushing more than anyone else. Self-sufficiency in meal, dependent on imported beans (USDA Oilseeds MY2024/25).

PRY.note: Major South American soybean-meal exporter (USDA MY2024/25 ~2.3-2.5 Mt). Landlocked; ships meal down the Parana-Paraguay river system, with destinations spanning the EU (UK, Poland, Italy), Chile, Peru, Brazil and Southeast Asia.

RUS.note: Fast-growing soybean- and sunflower-meal exporter (FAOSTAT/USDA 2024 ~1.5-1.8 Mt). Far-East crush ships soymeal to China; European-Russia crush exports sunflower meal to Turkey, Latvia and the EU. Sunflower meal is a lower-protein feed component.

UKR.note: World's leading sunflower-meal exporter and a growing soymeal shipper despite the war (FAOSTAT 2024 ~4+ Mt combined). Sunflower meal flows to the EU (Poland, France, Italy, Spain), China and Turkey; logistics constrained by Black Sea conditions.

NLD.note: Europe's primary oilseed-crush and meal-trading hub (Rotterdam). Imports South American beans and finished meal, crushes domestically and re-exports meal to Belgium, Germany, France and the wider EU. Both a large importer and a large intra-EU re-exporter (FAOSTAT 2024).

DEU.note: Major EU crusher (rapeseed/soybean) and a large net meal importer for its hog, poultry and dairy sectors. Sources Brazilian/Argentine soymeal plus Dutch and Polish re-exports; also exports rapeseed meal regionally. EU feed-protein demand keeps it structurally short (FAOSTAT 2024).

POL.note: One of the EU's largest soybean-meal importers, feeding a booming poultry industry (the EU's #1 poultry producer). Sources Argentine and Brazilian soymeal plus Ukrainian/Paraguayan supply. Almost entirely import-dependent for feed protein (FAOSTAT 2024).

FRA.note: Large EU livestock economy and rapeseed crusher; net importer of soybean meal for poultry, pork and dairy. Sources Brazilian/Argentine soymeal plus Ukrainian sunflower meal and Indian/Nigerian groundnut and other cakes (FAOSTAT 2024).

ESP.note: The EU's largest feed-compound producer and a top soybean-meal importer for its huge pork and poultry sectors. Major crush at coastal plants plus heavy imports of Brazilian/Argentine soymeal and Ukrainian sunflower meal (FAOSTAT 2024).

IDN.note: One of the world's largest soybean-meal importers (USDA MY2024/25 ~5.5-6 Mt) for its fast-growing poultry and aquaculture feed sectors. Sourced overwhelmingly from Brazil and Argentina; minimal domestic crush. A textbook meal-dependent feed economy.

VNM.note: Major Southeast Asian feed importer (USDA MY2024/25 soymeal imports ~5+ Mt) for its large pork, poultry and aquaculture industries. Sourced from Argentina, Brazil, the US and India. Did not separately report 2024 HS2304 detail to Comtrade at full granularity.

THA.note: Large poultry and aquaculture exporter that imports soybean meal to feed them (FAOSTAT 2024 imports ~3.5-4 Mt). Sourced chiefly from Brazil, plus India, Argentina, the US and Ukraine. A processed-protein exporter built on imported feed protein.

PHL.note: One of the largest US soybean-meal markets (USDA MY2024/25 imports ~3 Mt) for its hog and poultry sectors. The US is the dominant supplier (Western-Hemisphere logistics), with Argentina and Brazil filling in. Negligible domestic crush.

rankings.note: Oilseed cake/meal (HS2304 soybean meal + HS2306 rapeseed/canola meal + HS2305 groundnut cake + sunflower meal) volumes in kt, 2024, blending USDA Oilseeds MY2024/25 PSD with FAOSTAT 2024 importer-reports and India's SEA. Argentina is the world's #1 soybean-meal exporter (~27 Mt, 30-40% of global soymeal trade); Brazil and the US follow. Canada leads canola-meal exports (~4.5 Mt, chiefly to the US/China); India leads rapeseed/groundnut meal. The EU as a bloc is the largest importer (record ~22 Mt soymeal MY2024/25); Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand are the largest single-country buyers. Note: ranking values mix soybean meal with rapeseed/canola/sunflower/groundnut cake, so the basket totals exceed any single-meal series.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD' crush majors and among the world's largest oilseed processors; ~US$160bn revenue (FY2024). Operates soybean/rapeseed crush plants across the Americas and Europe producing meal for animal feed; also a leading feed/animal-nutrition company (Cargill Animal Nutrition).
companies.improve: Should publish plant-level deforestation-free soy sourcing verification (Cerrado/Amazon) and meal carbon intensity, given soy-driven land-use change in its South American supply base.

companies.name: Bunge Global
companies.note: The world's largest oilseed processor by crush capacity, now merged with Viterra (2024-25); ~US$53bn revenue. Soybean/rapeseed/sunflower crush across the Americas, Europe and the Black Sea is its core business — meal is the primary output by volume.
companies.improve: Should disclose full traceability to farm/municipality for South American soy meal and report progress against its deforestation-free 2025 commitment across indirect suppliers.

companies.name: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM)
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD' majors; ~US$85bn revenue (FY2024). Large soybean/rapeseed crush footprint in North America, South America and Europe; meal feeds its own animal-nutrition division and third-party feed mills.
companies.improve: Should report meal-level Scope 3 emissions and the share of crush volume from verified deforestation-free and regenerative-agriculture soy.

companies.name: COFCO International
companies.note: China's state-backed agri-trading giant and a major global crusher; the key channel feeding Chinese hog/poultry demand with imported beans turned into meal. Large origination in Brazil/Argentina and crush capacity in China (2024).
companies.improve: Should publish deforestation-free sourcing verification for its Brazilian soy origination and disclose how much of its meal supply meets EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) traceability.

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.note: The 'D' of the ABCD majors; a leading oilseed crusher and meal trader with major plants in Argentina (General Lagos, one of the world's largest crush complexes), Brazil and the US (2024).
companies.improve: Should disclose plant-level meal output traceability and the deforestation-risk profile of its Cerrado soy catchment, plus water use at its Argentine river-port crush hubs.

companies.name: Viterra
companies.note: Major oilseed handler/crusher (Canadian canola, Australian canola, Argentine soy), now combining with Bunge (2024-25). A leading exporter of Canadian canola meal to the US and China.
companies.improve: Should report canola-meal sourcing and the sustainability profile of its Canadian/Australian oilseed supply, and clarify post-merger concentration in global crush capacity.

global.note: World oilseed-meal totals, kt, blending USDA Oilseeds PSD (soybean meal ~260 Mt, rapeseed/canola meal ~45 Mt, sunflower meal ~25 Mt, plus groundnut/cottonseed/palm-kernel meal) with FAOSTAT 2024 trade. Soybean meal is ~70% of the basket. Global oilseed-meal trade reached ~110-112 Mt in 2024 (USDA: meal trade up >1.5 Mt to ~110 Mt on higher Argentina, Ukraine and China soymeal exports). Demand tracks global poultry/pork/dairy/aquaculture feed growth.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Protein-meal demand grows ~1.5-2%/yr with rising meat/dairy/aquaculture consumption in Asia and Africa; crush expansion led by Argentina, Brazil, the US (renewable-diesel-driven) and China, tempered by EUDR deforestation rules reshaping EU soymeal sourcing.
